nodes.summary: The claim of Problem 79 of the Scottish Book for the plane is false: there is a polynomial map $P$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ to itself with a polynomial two-sided inverse that is not of the form $x \mapsto Ax + c$ with $A$ an invertible real $2 \times 2$ matrix and $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$. For example, the map $(x_1, x_2) \mapsto (x_1, x_2 + x_1^2)$ has the inverse $(y_1, y_2) \mapsto (y_1, y_2 - y_1^2)$.
nodes.title: Mazur–Orlicz Problem 79 has a negative answer
